meta.topic: 线性代数：线性组合、线性相关、向量组的秩、基与坐标、齐次与非齐次线性方程组、秩–零化度定理

zh: 设 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^n$，$k_1,\dots,k_s\in\mathbb{R}$，则 $k_1\alpha_1+\cdots+k_s\alpha_s$ 称为这组向量的一个线性组合。取 $A=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s)$ 为以这些向量为列的 $n\times s$ 矩阵，$\boldsymbol{x}=(k_1,\dots,k_s)^{\mathrm T}$，按矩阵乘法定义 $A\boldsymbol{x}=k_1\alpha_1+\cdots+k_s\alpha_s$；所以「$\beta$ 可由 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s$ 线性表示」与「方程组 $A\boldsymbol{x}=\beta$ 有解」是同一句话，未知量就是待求的组合系数。

有解性由秩判定。对增广矩阵 $(A|\beta)$ 作初等行变换，不改变方程组的解集；化为行阶梯形后，若最后一列出现主元，就得到 $0=\text{非零数}$ 的矛盾方程，无解；若最后一列没有主元，则 $\beta$ 是前面各列（主元列）的线性组合，回代即得一组系数。因此 $\beta$ 可表示 $\iff r(A)=r(A|\beta)$，等价地 $\beta\in\operatorname{Col}(A)$。这里必须比较两个秩，只看 $r(A)$ 不够。

表示系数是否唯一取决于列向量是否线性无关。若 $\sum x_i\alpha_i=\sum y_i\alpha_i=\beta$，相减得 $\sum (x_i-y_i)\alpha_i=\boldsymbol{0}$。若 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s$ 线性无关，则所有 $x_i-y_i=0$，系数唯一；若它们线性相关，则存在非零向量 $\boldsymbol{z}$ 使 $A\boldsymbol{z}=\boldsymbol{0}$，于是 $\boldsymbol{x}+t\boldsymbol{z}$ 对任意 $t\in\mathbb{R}$ 都是系数解，表示不唯一（此时若有解就有无穷多组系数）。但系数不唯一不影响「能否表示」这一判断。

判断步骤可以固定为：写出 $(A|\beta)$，只用初等行变换化为行最简形；若最后一列有主元则不能表示；否则主元列对应的未知量由自由未知量表示，令自由未知量全为 0 即得一组系数。例如 $\alpha_1=(1,2,3)^{\mathrm T}$，$\alpha_2=(3,2,1)^{\mathrm T}$，$\beta=(4,4,4)^{\mathrm T}$，行化简得 $\begin{pmatrix}1&3&4\\0&1&1\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$，故 $r(A)=r(A|\beta)=2$，$y=1$、$x=1$，即 $\beta=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$，且因两列不成比例、线性无关，系数唯一。

线性表示具有传递性，并且与秩单调相容。若 $\gamma=\sum_{j=1}^t d_j\beta_j$ 且每个 $\beta_j=\sum_{i=1}^s c_{ij}\alpha_i$，代入得 $\gamma=\sum_{i=1}^s\left(\sum_{j=1}^t c_{ij}d_j\right)\alpha_i$，仍是 $\alpha$ 组的线性组合。矩阵语言即 $B=AC\Rightarrow r(B)\le r(A)$；特例是 $\beta$ 可表示时 $r(A|\beta)=r(A)$。这说明「添上可表示的向量不增加秩」。

两个向量组若互相可以线性表示，就称为等价；这等价于它们张成同一个子空间 $\operatorname{span}$，因而秩相等。反过来，仅有 $r(A)=r(B)$ 不能推出等价：$\mathbb{R}^3$ 中 $\{e_1,e_2\}$ 与 $\{e_1,e_3\}$ 的秩都为 2，但 $e_2$ 不能由 $\{e_1,e_3\}$ 表示。正确命题是：若 $B$ 可由 $A$ 表示且 $r(A)=r(B)$，则 $\operatorname{span}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{span}(A)$ 且维数相同，故两个子空间相等，$A,B$ 等价。表示、张成、秩、基与坐标，都是同一件事的不同说法。
en: Let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $k_1,\dots,k_s\in\mathbb{R}$. The vector $k_1\alpha_1+\cdots+k_s\alpha_s$ is called a linear combination of the group. Put $A=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s)$, the $n\times s$ matrix with these vectors as columns, and $\boldsymbol{x}=(k_1,\dots,k_s)^{\mathrm T}$. By the definition of matrix–vector multiplication, $A\boldsymbol{x}=k_1\alpha_1+\cdots+k_s\alpha_s$. Hence “$\beta$ is linearly representable by $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s$” and “the system $A\boldsymbol{x}=\beta$ is consistent” are the same statement, the unknowns being the coefficients sought.

Consistency is decided by ranks. Elementary row operations on the augmented matrix $(A|\beta)$ preserve the solution set. After reduction to row echelon form, a pivot in the last column yields an equation $0=\text{a nonzero number}$, so there is no solution; if the last column has no pivot, then $\beta$ is a linear combination of the preceding (pivot) columns, and back-substitution produces the coefficients. Therefore $\beta$ is representable iff $r(A)=r(A|\beta)$, equivalently $\beta\in\operatorname{Col}(A)$. Both ranks must be compared; knowing $r(A)$ alone is not enough.

Uniqueness of the coefficients is governed by linear independence of the columns. If $\sum x_i\alpha_i=\sum y_i\alpha_i=\beta$, subtraction gives $\sum (x_i-y_i)\alpha_i=\boldsymbol{0}$. When $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s$ are linearly independent, all $x_i-y_i=0$ and the coefficients are unique. When they are dependent, there is a nonzero $\boldsymbol{z}$ with $A\boldsymbol{z}=\boldsymbol{0}$, so $\boldsymbol{x}+t\boldsymbol{z}$ is a coefficient vector for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and the representation is not unique (if one exists, there are infinitely many). Non-uniqueness of coefficients does not affect the yes/no question of representability.

The standard procedure is: write $(A|\beta)$, reduce to reduced row echelon form using only elementary row operations; if the last column has a pivot, $\beta$ is not representable; otherwise express the pivot unknowns in terms of the free unknowns and set all free unknowns to 0 to obtain one coefficient vector. For example, with $\alpha_1=(1,2,3)^{\mathrm T}$, $\alpha_2=(3,2,1)^{\mathrm T}$, $\beta=(4,4,4)^{\mathrm T}$, reduction gives $\begin{pmatrix}1&3&4\\0&1&1\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$. Thus $r(A)=r(A|\beta)=2$, $y=1$ and $x=1$, so $\beta=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$; since the two columns are not proportional, they are independent and the coefficients are unique.

Linear representation is transitive and compatible with rank monotonicity. If $\gamma=\sum_{j=1}^t d_j\beta_j$ and each $\beta_j=\sum_{i=1}^s c_{ij}\alpha_i$, substitution gives $\gamma=\sum_{i=1}^s\left(\sum_{j=1}^t c_{ij}d_j\right)\alpha_i$, still a linear combination of the $\alpha$'s. In matrix form $B=AC\Rightarrow r(B)\le r(A)$; in particular, if $\beta$ is representable then $r(A|\beta)=r(A)$. Adjoining a representable vector adds no rank.

Two groups that represent each other are called equivalent; this is equivalent to their spanning the same subspace, and then their ranks are equal. Conversely, $r(A)=r(B)$ alone does not imply equivalence: in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\{e_1,e_2\}$ and $\{e_1,e_3\}$ both have rank 2, but $e_2$ is not representable by $\{e_1,e_3\}$. The correct statement is: if $B$ is representable by $A$ and $r(A)=r(B)$, then $\operatorname{span}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{span}(A)$ and the dimensions coincide, so the two spans are equal and $A,B$ are equivalent. Representation, spanning, rank, bases and coordinates are different ways of saying the same thing.

zh: 设 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^n$（$s\ge1$）。若存在不全为零的 $k_1,\dots,k_s$ 使 $\sum k_i\alpha_i=\boldsymbol{0}$，称向量组线性相关；若该等式强制 $k_1=\cdots=k_s=0$，称线性无关。注意系数全为零的平凡组合永远给出零向量，所以相关的关键是「还存在非平凡组合」。把向量按列排成 $A$，则 $\sum k_i\alpha_i=A\boldsymbol{k}$，相关 $\iff A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 有非零解。

齐次方程 $A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 的非零解由秩决定：$A$ 有 $s$ 列，行化简后有 $r(A)$ 个主元、$s-r(A)$ 个自由未知量；自由未知量取 1（其余取 0）就得到非零解，故有非零解 $\iff s-r(A)>0$。于是
$$\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\ \text{线性相关}\iff r(A)<s\iff A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}\ \text{有非零解};$$
线性无关 $\iff r(A)=s$。判断依据是秩与向量个数的比较，不是「系数是否互不相同」这类表面条件。

当 $s\ge2$ 时，相关还等价于「至少有一个向量能由其余向量表示」。若 $\sum k_i\alpha_i=0$ 且 $k_j

结构性质随之而来：相关组的任何扩大组仍相关（把原关系系数补零）；无关组的任何部分组仍无关（否则部分组的相关关系也是整组的相关关系）。含零向量的组必相关，因为给零向量配系数 1、其余配 0 即得非平凡零组合。$\mathbb{R}^n$ 中任意 $s>n$ 个向量必相关，因为 $r(A)\le n<s$。但反向不成立：整体相关推不出部分相关，例如 $(1,0)^{\mathrm T},(0,1)^{\mathrm T},(1,1)^{\mathrm T}$ 整体相关，任意两个却线性无关。

当 $s=n$（$n$ 个 $n$ 维向量）时，$A$ 为方阵，$A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 有非零解 $\iff\det A=0$，所以 $\det A\ne0$ 是它们线性无关的充要条件。例如 $\alpha_1=(1,1,1)^{\mathrm T}$，$\alpha_2=(1,2,3)^{\mathrm T}$，$\alpha_3=(1,3,5)^{\mathrm T}$，
$$\det A=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&3\\1&3&5\end{vmatrix}=1-2+1=0,$$
故三者相关；解 $k_1\alpha_1+k_2\alpha_2+k_3\alpha_3=0$ 得 $k_1=1,k_2=-2,k_3=1$，即 $\alpha_1-2\alpha_2+\alpha_3=\boldsymbol{0}$。验算成立。

标准检验流程是：把向量按列排成 $A$，解 $A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$（或对 $A$ 行化简数主元）。若 $r(A)=s$，无关；若 $r(A)<s$，相关，且自由未知量给出所有线性关系，取一组非零解即可写出一个具体关系式，并解出某个可被其余表示的向量。常见错误是把「两两不成比例」当成线性无关：上例中任意两个向量都不成比例，但三个向量整体相关；对 $s=2$，不成比例就是无关；对 $s\ge3$，两两不成比例远不足以保证整体无关。
en: Let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $s\ge1$. The group is linearly dependent if there exist coefficients $k_1,\dots,k_s$, not all zero, such that $\sum k_i\alpha_i=\boldsymbol{0}$; it is linearly independent if this identity forces $k_1=\cdots=k_s=0$. The trivial combination with all coefficients zero always gives the zero vector, so the point of dependence is the existence of a nontrivial combination. Arranging the vectors as the columns of $A$, $\sum k_i\alpha_i=A\boldsymbol{k}$, so dependence is equivalent to $A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ having a nonzero solution.

Nonzero solutions of $A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ are governed by rank: $A$ has $s$ columns, so after row reduction there are $r(A)$ pivots and $s-r(A)$ free unknowns; setting one free unknown to 1 and the others to 0 produces a nonzero solution. Hence a nonzero solution exists iff $s-r(A)>0$, and
$$\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\ \text{are dependent}\iff r(A)<s\iff A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}\ \text{has a nonzero solution};$$
they are independent iff $r(A)=s$. The test compares the rank with the number of vectors, not superficial features such as whether the coefficients differ.

For $s\ge2$, dependence is also equivalent to at least one vector being representable by the remaining ones. If $\sum k_i\alpha_i=0$ with $k_j
e0$, then $\alpha_j=-\sum_{i
e j}(k_i/k_j)\alpha_i$; conversely, if $\alpha_j=\sum_{i
e j}c_i\alpha_i$, then $\sum_{i
e j}c_i\alpha_i-\alpha_j= oldsymbol{0}$, a nontrivial relation because the coefficient of $\alpha_j$ is $-1$. The phrase is “at least one”, not “every one”: in a dependent group some vectors may fail to be representable by the others, but at least one is redundant.

Structural consequences follow. Any enlargement of a dependent group stays dependent (extend the relation by zero coefficients), and any sub-group of an independent group stays independent (otherwise the relation in the sub-group would be a relation in the whole group). A group containing the zero vector is dependent: assign coefficient 1 to the zero vector and 0 to the rest. Any $s>n$ vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are dependent because $r(A)\le n<s$. The converse does not hold: a dependent whole need not contain a dependent part; for example $(1,0)^{\mathrm T},(0,1)^{\mathrm T},(1,1)^{\mathrm T}$ are dependent as a triple, while every pair is independent.

When $s=n$ ($n$ vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$), $A$ is square and $A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ has a nonzero solution iff $\det A=0$; hence $\det A\ne0$ is necessary and sufficient for independence. For example, with $\alpha_1=(1,1,1)^{\mathrm T}$, $\alpha_2=(1,2,3)^{\mathrm T}$, $\alpha_3=(1,3,5)^{\mathrm T}$,
$$\det A=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&3\\1&3&5\end{vmatrix}=1-2+1=0,$$
so the three are dependent. Solving $k_1\alpha_1+k_2\alpha_2+k_3\alpha_3=0$ gives $k_1=1,k_2=-2,k_3=1$, i.e. $\alpha_1-2\alpha_2+\alpha_3=\boldsymbol{0}$, which checks directly.

The standard test is: form the column matrix $A$ and solve $A\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{0}$ (or count pivots in a row reduction of $A$). If $r(A)=s$, the group is independent; if $r(A)<s$, it is dependent, the free unknowns parametrize all linear relations, and one nonzero solution yields an explicit relation from which a redundant vector can be solved for. A common mistake is to treat “no two vectors are proportional” as independence: in the example above every pair is non-proportional, yet the triple is dependent. For $s=2$, non-proportionality is exactly independence; for $s\ge3$, pairwise non-proportionality is far from sufficient for independence of the whole group.

zh: 设 $T=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\}$ 是有限向量组。若其中一部分 $\alpha_{i_1},\dots,\alpha_{i_r}$ 满足：（1）线性无关；（2）$T$ 中每个向量都可由它们线性表示，则称之为 $T$ 的最大线性无关组，简称最大无关组，$r$ 称为 $T$ 的秩，记 $r(T)$。条件（2）保证没有向量被遗漏。有限组一定存在最大无关组：从空集开始，只要当前无关组不能张成整个 $T$，就取一个不在其张成空间中的向量添入，无关性保持而向量个数增加，有限步后停止。

最大无关组也可以刻画为「加不进新向量的线性无关部分组」。若 $\beta\in T$ 不在 $\operatorname{span}(\alpha_{i_1},\dots,\alpha_{i_r})$ 中，设 $c\beta+\sum c_j\alpha_{i_j}=0$；若 $c\ne0$，则 $\beta$ 可由这些 $\alpha$ 表示，矛盾，故 $c=0$，再由无关性得所有 $c_j=0$。所以加上 $\beta$ 仍无关；反之，若存在向量不能由该组表示，就还能扩充。两种定义因此等价，且最大无关组张成 $T$，而 $T$ 本身包含这些向量、故可表示其中每一个，所以两者等价。

秩的良定义性需要证明任意两个最大无关组含向量个数相同。设 $A=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$ 与 $B=\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_t\}$ 都是 $T$ 的最大无关组。它们都张成 $T$，故互相可表示。若 $t<r$，把 $A=BC$ 写成矩阵形式，则 $r(A)\le r(B)\le t$；但 $A$ 线性无关，$r(A)=r$，矛盾。对称地 $r<t$ 也不可能，故 $r=t$。因此最大无关组可以更换，秩却唯一，记这个公共数为 $r(T)$。

秩与矩阵秩是同一个量。把向量按列排成 $A=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s)$，则 $r(T)=r(A)$。求法：对 $A$ 作初等行变换化为行最简形。行变换相当于左乘可逆矩阵 $E$，$A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}\iff EA\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$，所以列向量之间的线性关系完全保留；行最简形的主元列线性无关，非主元列由主元列唯一表示。于是原矩阵中主元位置对应的那些列构成一个最大无关组，非主元列的表示系数可直接从行最简形读出。

基本不等式：$r(T)\le s$（最大无关组是原组的一部分）且 $r(T)\le n$（$T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$）；$r(T)=s\iff T$ 线性无关。若向量组 $B$ 可由 $A$ 表示，则 $r(B)\le r(A)$。进一步，若还有 $r(A)=r(B)$，则 $\operatorname{span}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{span}(A)$ 且维数相等，故两子空间相等，$A$ 与 $B$ 等价。仅凭秩相等不能推出等价，必须有「一组能表示另一组」这一前提。

例：$\alpha_1=(1,1,1)^{\mathrm T}$，$\alpha_2=(1,2,3)^{\mathrm T}$，$\alpha_3=(3,4,5)^{\mathrm T}$。观察 $\alpha_3=2\alpha_1+\alpha_2$（验算：$(2,2,2)+(1,2,3)=(3,4,5)$），故 $\alpha_3$ 冗余，$r\le2$；又 $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ 不成比例，线性无关，所以 $r=2$，$\{\alpha_1,\alpha_2\}$ 是一个最大无关组。由于 $\alpha_3$ 不是 $\alpha_1$ 或 $\alpha_2$ 的倍数，$\{\alpha_1,\alpha_3\}$、$\{\alpha_2,\alpha_3\}$ 也都无关，故全部最大无关组是这三对。最大无关组不唯一，秩 2 唯一。
en: Let $T=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s\}$ be a finite group of vectors. A sub-group $\alpha_{i_1},\dots,\alpha_{i_r}$ is a maximal linearly independent subset (maximal independent subset) of $T$ if (i) it is linearly independent and (ii) every vector of $T$ is representable by it; the number $r$ is the rank $r(T)$. Condition (ii) says no vector is left out. A maximal independent subset always exists for a finite group: start with the empty set and, whenever the current independent set does not span all of $T$, add a vector of $T$ lying outside its span; independence is preserved and the size grows, so the process stops after finitely many steps.

Equivalently, a maximal independent subset is an independent sub-group to which no further vector of $T$ can be added while preserving independence. If $\beta\in T$ lies outside $\operatorname{span}(\alpha_{i_1},\dots,\alpha_{i_r})$ and $c\beta+\sum c_j\alpha_{i_j}=0$, then $c\ne0$ would express $\beta$ through the $\alpha$'s, a contradiction; hence $c=0$, and independence of the $\alpha$'s forces all $c_j=0$. Thus adjoining $\beta$ keeps independence. Conversely, if some vector of $T$ is not representable, the set can still be enlarged. The two definitions agree, and a maximal independent subset spans $T$ while $T$ itself contains these vectors and therefore represents each of them, so the two groups are equivalent.

Well-definedness of the rank requires proving that any two maximal independent subsets have the same size. Let $A=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$ and $B=\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_t\}$ both be maximal independent subsets of $T$. Each spans $T$, so each is representable by the other. If $t<r$, writing $A=BC$ in matrix form gives $r(A)\le r(B)\le t$; but $A$ is independent, so $r(A)=r$, a contradiction. Symmetrically $r<t$ is impossible, hence $r=t$. Thus maximal independent subsets may change, but the rank is unique; this common number is $r(T)$.

The rank of a vector group is the same quantity as the rank of a matrix. Arrange the vectors as the columns of $A=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_s)$; then $r(T)=r(A)$. To compute it, reduce $A$ to reduced row echelon form. A row operation is left multiplication by an invertible matrix $E$, and $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}\iff EA\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$, so all linear relations among the columns are preserved. In the reduced form the pivot columns are independent and every non-pivot column is uniquely expressible through them. Therefore the original columns at the pivot positions form a maximal independent subset, and the coefficients expressing the other columns are read off directly from the reduced form.

Basic inequalities: $r(T)\le s$ (a maximal independent subset is part of the original group) and $r(T)\le n$ (since $T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$); moreover $r(T)=s$ iff $T$ is linearly independent. If a group $B$ is representable by $A$, then $r(B)\le r(A)$. If in addition $r(A)=r(B)$, then $\operatorname{span}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{span}(A)$ and the dimensions are equal, so the spans coincide and $A,B$ are equivalent. Equal ranks alone do not imply equivalence; the hypothesis that one group represents the other is indispensable.

Example: $\alpha_1=(1,1,1)^{\mathrm T}$, $\alpha_2=(1,2,3)^{\mathrm T}$, $\alpha_3=(3,4,5)^{\mathrm T}$. Observe $\alpha_3=2\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ (check: $(2,2,2)+(1,2,3)=(3,4,5)$), so $\alpha_3$ is redundant and $r\le2$. Since $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ are not proportional, they are independent, hence $r=2$ and $\{\alpha_1,\alpha_2\}$ is a maximal independent subset. Because $\alpha_3$ is not a multiple of $\alpha_1$ or of $\alpha_2$, the pairs $\{\alpha_1,\alpha_3\}$ and $\{\alpha_2,\alpha_3\}$ are also independent, so all three pairs are maximal independent subsets. The maximal independent subset is not unique, but the rank 2 is unique.

zh: 设 $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ 非空，且对加法与数乘封闭，则 $V$ 是子空间。若 $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r\in V$ 线性无关，且 $V$ 中每个向量都可由它们表示，就称它们为 $V$ 的一组基，$r=\dim V$。$\mathbb{R}^n$ 的标准基 $e_1,\dots,e_n$ 给出 $\dim\mathbb{R}^n=n$；零子空间 $\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ 的基是空集，维数为 0。由定义，基正是把 $V$ 看作向量组时的最大无关组，维数就是该向量组的秩。

坐标的唯一性由基的线性无关性直接推出。若 $\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^r x_i\varepsilon_i=\sum_{i=1}^r y_i\varepsilon_i$，相减得 $\sum (x_i-y_i)\varepsilon_i=\boldsymbol{0}$，无关性迫使 $x_i=y_i$。因此映射 $\alpha\mapsto(x_1,\dots,x_r)^{\mathrm T}$ 是良定义的；它还是线性的，并且由「基张成 $V$」得满射、由「基无关」得单射，所以是 $V\to\mathbb{R}^r$ 的线性同构。特别地，零向量的坐标必为 $(0,\dots,0)^{\mathrm T}$。
维数与基的选择无关。$V$ 的任意两组基都是 $V$ 的最大无关组，由上一节点的结论，它们含向量个数相同，都等于 $r(V)$。因此 $\dim V$ 是 $V$ 自身的不变量；除零子空间外，基可以有无穷多组。这里 $V$ 必须是子空间：不过原点的直线或平面不满足对加法封闭，也不含零向量，因而没有这种线性结构。

基的判定有几种常用形式。设 $\dim V=r$，并记住两个基本事实：$V$ 中任何线性无关组至多含 $r$ 个向量，任何张成组至少含 $r$ 个向量（否则通过扩充或删减会得到与维数定义矛盾的基）。① $V$ 中任意 $r$ 个线性无关的向量都构成基：它们张成 $r$ 维子空间 $U\subseteq V$，若 $U\ne V$，取 $\alpha\in V\setminus U$，则这 $r$ 个向量加 $\alpha$ 仍线性无关，得到 $V$ 中 $r+1$ 个无关向量，与第一个事实矛盾。② $V$ 中任意 $r$ 个能张成 $V$ 的向量都构成基：若它们相关，删去一个冗余向量仍张成 $V$，得到少于 $r$ 个向量的张成组，与第二个事实矛盾。③ 无关组可扩充为基，张成组可删减为基。

在 $r$ 维子空间 $V$ 中取定旧基 $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r$ 与新基 $\varepsilon'_1,\dots,\varepsilon'_r$，设
$$(\varepsilon'_1,\dots,\varepsilon'_r)=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r)P,\qquad P=(p_{ij}),$$
即 $\varepsilon'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}\varepsilon_i$，$P$ 的第 $j$ 列是新基向量在旧基下的坐标。若 $\alpha=\sum_j x'_j\varepsilon'_j$，代入得
$$\alpha=\sum_i\left(\sum_j p_{ij}x'_j\right)\varepsilon_i=\sum_i(P\boldsymbol{x}')_i\varepsilon_i.$$
由旧基下坐标唯一，$\boldsymbol{x}=P\boldsymbol{x}'$，故 $\boldsymbol{x}'=P^{-1}\boldsymbol{x}$。$P$ 可逆是因为新基线性无关。方向不能写反：$P$ 的列是新基在旧基下的坐标，不是旧基在新基下的坐标。

例：$\mathbb{R}^2$ 中取基 $\varepsilon_1=(1,2)^{\mathrm T}$，$\varepsilon_2=(2,5)^{\mathrm T}$，求 $\beta=(4,9)^{\mathrm T}$ 的坐标。设 $\beta=x\varepsilon_1+y\varepsilon_2$，得 $x+2y=4$，$2x+5y=9$，解得 $y=1,x=2$，故坐标为 $(2,1)^{\mathrm T}$。用换基公式核对：$P=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{pmatrix}$，$\det P=1$，$P^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix}$，于是 $\boldsymbol{x}'=P^{-1}(4,9)^{\mathrm T}=(2,1)^{\mathrm T}$。同一个向量在标准基下坐标是 $(4,9)^{\mathrm T}$，在新基下是 $(2,1)^{\mathrm T}$：向量本身不变，坐标随基改变。
en: Let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty and closed under addition and scalar multiplication; then $V$ is a subspace. Vectors $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r\in V$ form a basis of $V$ if they are linearly independent and every vector of $V$ is representable by them; then $r=\dim V$. The standard basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ gives $\dim\mathbb{R}^n=n$, while the zero subspace $\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ has the empty basis and dimension 0. By definition, a basis is exactly a maximal independent subset of $V$ regarded as a vector group, and the dimension is its rank.

Uniqueness of coordinates follows directly from independence of the basis. If $\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^r x_i\varepsilon_i=\sum_{i=1}^r y_i\varepsilon_i$, subtraction gives $\sum (x_i-y_i)\varepsilon_i=\boldsymbol{0}$, and independence forces $x_i=y_i$. Hence the map $\alpha\mapsto(x_1,\dots,x_r)^{\mathrm T}$ is well defined. It is linear, surjective because the basis spans $V$, and injective because the basis is independent; therefore it is a linear isomorphism $V\to\mathbb{R}^r$. In particular, the zero vector has coordinates $(0,\dots,0)^{\mathrm T}$.

The dimension does not depend on the choice of basis. Any two bases of $V$ are maximal independent subsets of $V$, so by the preceding node they contain the same number of vectors, namely $r(V)$. Thus $\dim V$ is an invariant of $V$ itself; apart from the zero subspace, $V$ has infinitely many bases. Here $V$ must be a subspace: a line or plane not passing through the origin is not closed under addition and does not contain the zero vector, so it has no linear structure of this kind.

There are several standard criteria for a basis. Let $\dim V=r$, and recall two basic facts: any linearly independent set in $V$ has at most $r$ vectors, and any spanning set has at least $r$ vectors (otherwise extension or deletion would produce a basis contradicting the definition of dimension). (i) Any $r$ linearly independent vectors in $V$ form a basis: they span an $r$-dimensional subspace $U\subseteq V$; if $U\ne V$, choose $\alpha\in V\setminus U$, and the $r$ vectors together with $\alpha$ are still independent, giving $r+1$ independent vectors in $V$, contradicting the first fact. (ii) Any $r$ vectors in $V$ that span $V$ form a basis: if they were dependent, deleting a redundant vector would leave a spanning set with fewer than $r$ vectors, contradicting the second fact. (iii) An independent set can be extended to a basis, and a spanning set can be trimmed to a basis.

In the $r$-dimensional subspace $V$ fix an old basis $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r$ and a new basis $\varepsilon'_1,\dots,\varepsilon'_r$, and write
$$(\varepsilon'_1,\dots,\varepsilon'_r)=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_r)P,\qquad P=(p_{ij}),$$
so $\varepsilon'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}\varepsilon_i$: the $j$-th column of $P$ holds the coordinates of the new basis vector in the old basis. If $\alpha=\sum_j x'_j\varepsilon'_j$, substitution gives
$$\alpha=\sum_i\left(\sum_j p_{ij}x'_j\right)\varepsilon_i=\sum_i(P\boldsymbol{x}')_i\varepsilon_i.$$
By uniqueness of old coordinates, $\boldsymbol{x}=P\boldsymbol{x}'$, hence $\boldsymbol{x}'=P^{-1}\boldsymbol{x}$. The matrix $P$ is invertible because the new basis is independent. The direction is easy to reverse by mistake: the columns of $P$ are the new basis vectors in the old basis, not the old ones in the new basis.

Example: in $\mathbb{R}^2$ take the basis $\varepsilon_1=(1,2)^{\mathrm T}$, $\varepsilon_2=(2,5)^{\mathrm T}$ and find the coordinates of $\beta=(4,9)^{\mathrm T}$. Writing $\beta=x\varepsilon_1+y\varepsilon_2$ gives $x+2y=4$, $2x+5y=9$, hence $y=1,x=2$ and coordinates $(2,1)^{\mathrm T}$. Check with the change-of-basis formula: $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{pmatrix}$, $\det P=1$, $P^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix}$, so $\boldsymbol{x}'=P^{-1}(4,9)^{\mathrm T}=(2,1)^{\mathrm T}$. The same vector has standard coordinates $(4,9)^{\mathrm T}$ and new coordinates $(2,1)^{\mathrm T}$: the vector is unchanged, its coordinates change with the basis.

zh: 设 $A$ 为 $m\times n$ 实矩阵，齐次方程组 $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 的未知向量 $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$。$\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 永远是解。若 $A\boldsymbol{x}_1=\boldsymbol{0}$、$A\boldsymbol{x}_2=\boldsymbol{0}$，则 $A(\boldsymbol{x}_1+\boldsymbol{x}_2)=\boldsymbol{0}$、$A(k\boldsymbol{x}_1)=kA\boldsymbol{x}_1=\boldsymbol{0}$，所以解集对加法与数乘封闭；它非空且含零向量，从而是 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 的子空间，称为解空间或零空间 $N(A)$。

解空间的大小由秩决定。把 $A$ 行化简为行最简形，设 $r(A)=r$，则有 $r$ 个主元列、$n-r$ 个非主元列。主元对应的变量由自由变量唯一表示；令某个自由变量为 1、其余自由变量为 0，就得到一个非零解。因此 $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 有非零解 $\iff n-r>0\iff r(A)<n$；当 $r(A)=n$ 时没有自由变量，只有零解。特别地，$m<n$ 时 $r(A)\le m<n$，必有非零解。

进一步，$\dim N(A)=n-r(A)$，而且可以显式写出基。对每个自由变量 $x_{f_j}$，令它等于 1、其余自由变量等于 0，解出主变量，得到解 $\eta_j$（$j=1,\dots,n-r$）。这 $n-r$ 个解线性无关：若 $\sum k_j\eta_j=\boldsymbol{0}$，只看自由坐标就得到 $k_j=0$。它们也张成 $N(A)$：任取解 $\boldsymbol{x}$，减去 $\sum x_{f_j}\eta_j$ 后所有自由坐标为零，而主变量又被自由变量唯一决定，故差向量为零。因此 $\{\eta_1,\dots,\eta_{n-r}\}$ 是 $N(A)$ 的一组基。

取 $N(A)$ 的一组基 $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_{n-r}$，称为齐次方程组的一个基础解系：它们是 $n-r$ 个线性无关的解，且每个解都能由它们线性表示。通解为
$$\boldsymbol{x}=k_1\eta_1+\cdots+k_{n-r}\eta_{n-r},\qquad k_1,\dots,k_{n-r}\in\mathbb{R}.$$
由于基线性无关，给定解的系数还是唯一的。基础解系不唯一（解空间的任何一组基都可以），但所含向量个数 $n-r(A)$ 唯一确定；$r(A)=n$ 时基础解系为空，通解只有 $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$。

从矩阵语言看，$N(A)$ 的维数就是 $A$ 的零化度，$r(A)+\dim N(A)=n$。若 $A$ 的列向量为 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$，则 $\boldsymbol{x}\in N(A)$ 正好给出列向量之间的一组线性关系 $\sum x_i\alpha_i=\boldsymbol{0}$；因此列向量线性相关 $\iff N(A)\ne\{\boldsymbol{0}\}\iff r(A)<n$。这也说明：齐次方程的非零解、列向量组的线性相关、秩小于列数，是同一事实的三种表述。
en: Let $A$ be an $m\times n$ real matrix and consider $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$. The zero vector is always a solution. If $A\boldsymbol{x}_1=\boldsymbol{0}$ and $A\boldsymbol{x}_2=\boldsymbol{0}$, then $A(\boldsymbol{x}_1+\boldsymbol{x}_2)=\boldsymbol{0}$ and $A(k\boldsymbol{x}_1)=kA\boldsymbol{x}_1=\boldsymbol{0}$, so the solution set is closed under addition and scalar multiplication. It is nonempty and contains the zero vector, hence is a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$, called the solution space or null space $N(A)$.

The size of the solution space is controlled by the rank. Reduce $A$ to reduced row echelon form and let $r(A)=r$; there are $r$ pivot columns and $n-r$ non-pivot columns. Each pivot variable is uniquely determined by the free variables; setting one free variable to 1 and the others to 0 produces a nonzero solution. Therefore $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ has a nonzero solution iff $n-r>0$ iff $r(A)<n$; if $r(A)=n$ there are no free variables and only the zero solution. In particular, when $m<n$ we have $r(A)\le m<n$, so a nonzero solution must exist.

Moreover $\dim N(A)=n-r(A)$, and a basis can be written explicitly. For each free variable $x_{f_j}$, set it equal to 1 and the other free variables to 0, then solve for the pivot variables; this gives a solution $\eta_j$ ($j=1,\dots,n-r$). These $n-r$ solutions are independent: if $\sum k_j\eta_j=\boldsymbol{0}$, looking only at the free coordinates yields $k_j=0$. They span $N(A)$: given any solution $\boldsymbol{x}$, subtract $\sum x_{f_j}\eta_j$; the difference has all free coordinates zero, and since the pivot variables are uniquely determined by the free ones, the difference is zero. Hence $\{\eta_1,\dots,\eta_{n-r}\}$ is a basis of $N(A)$.

A basis $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_{n-r}$ of $N(A)$ is called a fundamental system of solutions of the homogeneous system: it consists of $n-r$ independent solutions, and every solution is a linear combination of them. The general solution is
$$\boldsymbol{x}=k_1\eta_1+\cdots+k_{n-r}\eta_{n-r},\qquad k_1,\dots,k_{n-r}\in\mathbb{R}.$$
Because the basis is independent, the coefficients of a given solution are unique. A fundamental system is not unique (any basis of the solution space qualifies), but the number of vectors, $n-r(A)$, is uniquely determined; when $r(A)=n$ the fundamental system is empty and the only solution is $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$.

Example: solve $x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4=0$, $x_1+2x_2+3x_3+4x_4=0$. Row reduction of the coefficient matrix gives
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&1\\1&2&3&4\end{pmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1&-2\\0&1&2&3\end{pmatrix},$$
so $r(A)=2$ and $\dim N(A)=4-2=2$. The pivot variables satisfy $x_1=x_3+2x_4$ and $x_2=-2x_3-3x_4$. Setting $(x_3,x_4)=(1,0)$ gives $\eta_1=(1,-2,1,0)^{\mathrm T}$; setting $(0,1)$ gives $\eta_2=(2,-3,0,1)^{\mathrm T}$. The general solution is $\boldsymbol{x}=k_1\eta_1+k_2\eta_2$.

In matrix language, $\dim N(A)$ is the nullity of $A$ and $r(A)+\dim N(A)=n$. If the columns of $A$ are $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$, then each $\boldsymbol{x}\in N(A)$ is exactly a linear relation $\sum x_i\alpha_i=\boldsymbol{0}$ among the columns; hence the columns are dependent iff $N(A)\ne\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ iff $r(A)<n$. Thus a nonzero solution of the homogeneous system, linear dependence of the columns, and rank less than the number of columns are three descriptions of one and the same fact.

zh:
设 $A$ 为 $m\times n$ 矩阵，$\boldsymbol{b}\ne\boldsymbol{0}$，方程组 $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ 的增广矩阵为 $(A|\boldsymbol{b})$。对增广矩阵作初等行变换，解集不变。化为行阶梯形后，若最后一列出现主元，就会出现形如 $0=d$（$d\ne0$）的方程，无解；若最后一列没有主元，则 $\boldsymbol{b}$ 可由 $A$ 的列向量表示，回代可得解。因此
$$A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}\ \text{有解}\iff r(A)=r(A|\boldsymbol{b}),$$
等价地 $\boldsymbol{b}\in\operatorname{Col}(A)$。由于只多一列，必有 $r(A)\le r(A|\boldsymbol{b})\le r(A)+1$；无解时恰有 $r(A|\boldsymbol{b})=r(A)+1$。

有解时解的个数由 $r=r(A)=r(A|\boldsymbol{b})$ 与未知数个数 $n$ 决定。行最简形有 $r$ 个主元、$n-r$ 个自由变量：若 $r=n$，没有自由变量，解唯一；若 $r<n$，自由变量可任意取值，得到一个含 $n-r$ 个参数的无穷解族。合起来就是三种互斥情形：$r=n$ 唯一解；$r<n$ 无穷多解；$r(A)<r(A|\boldsymbol{b})$ 无解（此时上面已证增广秩恰为大 1）。

解的结构由「特解 + 齐次解」给出。设 $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ 是 $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ 的一个特解，$\eta\in N(A)$。则
$$A(\boldsymbol{x}^*+\eta)=A\boldsymbol{x}^*+A\eta=\boldsymbol{b}+\boldsymbol{0}=\boldsymbol{b},$$
故 $\boldsymbol{x}^*+\eta$ 仍是解。反过来，若 $\boldsymbol{x}$ 也是解，则 $A(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{x}^*)=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{b}=\boldsymbol{0}$，即 $\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{x}^*=\eta\in N(A)$，于是 $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}^*+\eta$。因此解集恰为
$$\{\boldsymbol{x}:A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}\}=\boldsymbol{x}^*+N(A),$$
它是把解空间沿 $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ 平移得到的仿射子空间；$\boldsymbol{b}\ne\boldsymbol{0}$ 时零向量不是解，所以解集本身不是向量空间。

取导出组 $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ 的基础解系 $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_{n-r}$，非齐次方程组的通解为
$$\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}^*+k_1\eta_1+\cdots+k_{n-r}\eta_{n-r},\qquad k_i\in\mathbb{R}.$$
这里 $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ 是任意一个特解，$k_i$ 任意；改变特解只改变公式中的常数项，不改变解集。求法固定为三步：先对增广矩阵行化简并由两秩判断有解性，再解导出组得基础解系，最后令自由变量全为 0（或任取方便值）解出主变量得到一个特解，相加即得通解。

任意两个解之差是齐次解：若 $A\boldsymbol{x}_1=\boldsymbol{b}$、$A\boldsymbol{x}_2=\boldsymbol{b}$，则 $A(\boldsymbol{x}_1-\boldsymbol{x}_2)=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{b}=\boldsymbol{0}$。因此已知多个特解时，两两相减即可造出 $N(A)$ 中的向量；若能找到 $n-r$ 个线性无关的差向量，它们就构成导出组的基础解系，再取其中一个解作特解即可写出通解。注意差向量必须线性无关且个数达到 $n-r$，仅有一个差向量不能张成整个解空间。

例：解 $x_1+x_2+x_3=1$，$x_1+2x_2+3x_3=3$，$2x_1+3x_2+4x_3=4$。对增广矩阵行化简：
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&1\\1&2&3&3\\2&3&4&4\end{pmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&1&2&2\\0&0&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$
故 $r(A)=r(A|\boldsymbol{b})=2<3$，有无穷多解。由 $x_2+2x_3=2$、$x_1+x_2+x_3=1$ 得 $x_2=2-2x_3$，$x_1=-1+x_3$。令 $x_3=0$ 得特解 $\boldsymbol{x}^*=(-1,2,0)^{\mathrm T}$；导出组令 $x_3=1$ 得 $\eta=(1,-2,1)^{\mathrm T}$。通解 $\boldsymbol{x}=(-1,2,0)^{\mathrm T}+k(1,-2,1)^{\mathrm T}$，$k\in\mathbb{R}$。验算：$A\boldsymbol{x}^*=(1,3,4)^{\mathrm T}$，$A\eta=\boldsymbol{0}$。
en:
Let $A$ be $m\times n$, $\boldsymbol{b}\ne\boldsymbol{0}$, and let $(A|\boldsymbol{b})$ be the augmented matrix of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$. Elementary row operations on the augmented matrix preserve the solution set. After reduction to row echelon form, a pivot in the last column produces an equation $0=d$ with $d\ne0$, so there is no solution; if the last column has no pivot, then $\boldsymbol{b}$ is representable by the columns of $A$ and back-substitution gives a solution. Therefore
$$A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}\ \text{is consistent}\iff r(A)=r(A|\boldsymbol{b}),$$
equivalently $\boldsymbol{b}\in\operatorname{Col}(A)$. Since only one column is added, $r(A)\le r(A|\boldsymbol{b})\le r(A)+1$; in the inconsistent case $r(A|\boldsymbol{b})=r(A)+1$ exactly.

When the system is consistent, the number of solutions is determined by $r=r(A)=r(A|\boldsymbol{b})$ and the number $n$ of unknowns. The reduced row echelon form has $r$ pivots and $n-r$ free variables: if $r=n$ there are no free variables and the solution is unique; if $r<n$ the free variables are arbitrary and give an infinite family with $n-r$ parameters. Thus there are three mutually exclusive cases: $r=n$ gives a unique solution; $r<n$ gives infinitely many; $r(A)<r(A|\boldsymbol{b})$ gives no solution (and then the augmented rank is exactly one larger).

The structure of the solution set is “particular solution plus homogeneous solution”. Let $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ be a particular solution of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\eta\in N(A)$. Then
$$A(\boldsymbol{x}^*+\eta)=A\boldsymbol{x}^*+A\eta=\boldsymbol{b}+\boldsymbol{0}=\boldsymbol{b},$$
so $\boldsymbol{x}^*+\eta$ is again a solution. Conversely, if $\boldsymbol{x}$ is any solution, then $A(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{x}^*)=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{b}=\boldsymbol{0}$, so $\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{x}^*=\eta\in N(A)$ and $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}^*+\eta$. Hence the solution set is exactly
$$\{\boldsymbol{x}:A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}\}=\boldsymbol{x}^*+N(A),$$
the null space translated by $\boldsymbol{x}^*$, an affine subspace. When $\boldsymbol{b}\ne\boldsymbol{0}$ the zero vector is not a solution, so the solution set itself is not a vector space.

Taking a fundamental system $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_{n-r}$ of the associated homogeneous system $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$, the general solution of the nonhomogeneous system is
$$\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}^*+k_1\eta_1+\cdots+k_{n-r}\eta_{n-r},\qquad k_i\in\mathbb{R}.$$
Here $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is any particular solution and the $k_i$ are arbitrary; changing the particular solution changes only the constant term in the formula, not the solution set. The recipe has three steps: row-reduce the augmented matrix and use the two ranks to decide consistency; solve the associated homogeneous system for a fundamental system; set the free variables to 0 (or any convenient values), solve for the pivot variables to get one particular solution, and add.

The difference of any two solutions is homogeneous: if $A\boldsymbol{x}_1=\boldsymbol{b}$ and $A\boldsymbol{x}_2=\boldsymbol{b}$, then $A(\boldsymbol{x}_1-\boldsymbol{x}_2)=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{b}=\boldsymbol{0}$. Therefore, when several particular solutions are known, their pairwise differences produce vectors in $N(A)$; if one can find $n-r$ independent difference vectors, they form a fundamental system of the associated homogeneous system, and together with any one of the known solutions they yield the general solution. The differences must be independent and must number $n-r$; a single difference vector cannot span the whole solution space.

Example: solve $x_1+x_2+x_3=1$, $x_1+2x_2+3x_3=3$, $2x_1+3x_2+4x_3=4$. Row reduction of the augmented matrix gives
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&1\\1&2&3&3\\2&3&4&4\end{pmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&1&2&2\\0&0&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$
so $r(A)=r(A|\boldsymbol{b})=2<3$ and there are infinitely many solutions. From $x_2+2x_3=2$ and $x_1+x_2+x_3=1$ we get $x_2=2-2x_3$ and $x_1=-1+x_3$. Setting $x_3=0$ gives the particular solution $\boldsymbol{x}^*=(-1,2,0)^{\mathrm T}$; for the associated homogeneous system, setting $x_3=1$ gives $\eta=(1,-2,1)^{\mathrm T}$. The general solution is $\boldsymbol{x}=(-1,2,0)^{\mathrm T}+k(1,-2,1)^{\mathrm T}$, $k\in\mathbb{R}$. Check: $A\boldsymbol{x}^*=(1,3,4)^{\mathrm T}$ and $A\eta=\boldsymbol{0}$.

zh:
设 $V,W$ 是数域上的线性空间，$T:V\to W$ 线性。核与像定义为
$$\ker T=\{\alpha\in V:T(\alpha)=\boldsymbol{0}\},\qquad \operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}.$$
核是 $V$ 的子空间：$T(\boldsymbol{0})=\boldsymbol{0}$，且 $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=\boldsymbol{0}$。像是 $W$ 的子空间：$kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=T(k\alpha+l\beta)$ 仍是某个向量的像。$\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ 称为 $T$ 的秩，$\dim\ker T$ 称为零化度。

维数定理：若 $V$ 有限维，$\dim V=n$，则
$$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n.$$
证明：设 $\dim\ker T=k$，取核的基 $u_1,\dots,u_k$，由基扩充定理把它扩充为 $V$ 的基 $u_1,\dots,u_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$。先证 $T(v_1),\dots,T(v_{n-k})$ 张成 $\operatorname{Im}T$：任取 $T(x)$，写 $x=\sum a_i u_i+\sum b_j v_j$，则 $T(x)=\sum b_jT(v_j)$。再证它们无关：若 $\sum c_jT(v_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$，则 $T(\sum c_jv_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$，故 $\sum c_jv_j\in\ker T$，可写成 $\sum a_i u_i$；由 $V$ 的基无关性得所有 $c_j=0$。所以它们是 $\operatorname{Im}T$ 的基，$\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n-k$，定理成立。

矩阵版本是同一结论的坐标化。$m\times n$ 矩阵 $A$ 定义 $T_A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$，$T_A(\boldsymbol{x})=A\boldsymbol{x}$。此时 $\operatorname{Im}T_A=\{A\boldsymbol{x}:\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\}=\operatorname{Col}(A)$，故 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T_A=r(A)$；而 $\ker T_A=N(A)$ 正是齐次方程组的解空间。代入维数定理得
$$r(A)+\dim N(A)=n,\qquad \dim N(A)=n-r(A).$$
右边是 $n$（列数、未知数个数），不是 $m$（行数、方程个数）；这是最常见的记错点。

维数定理给出单射与满射的判别。$T$ 单射 $\iff\ker T=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$：若单射且 $T(\alpha)=0=T(0)$，则 $\alpha=0$；反之若核为零且 $T(\alpha)=T(\beta)$，则 $T(\alpha-\beta)=0$，故 $\alpha=\beta$。$T$ 满射 $\iff\operatorname{Im}T=W$，有限维时等价于 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W$。当 $\dim V=\dim W=n<\infty$ 时，结合 $\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n$ 得：单射 $\iff\dim\ker T=0\iff\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n\iff$ 满射 $\iff T$ 可逆。维数不同的有限维空间没有这个等价链：此时单射与满射一般不能互推。

两个模型可以直接核对。投影 $P:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$，$P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$：$\ker P=\{(0,0,z)\}$ 是 $z$ 轴，维数 1；$\operatorname{Im}P=\{(x,y,0)\}$ 是 $xy$ 平面，维数 2；$1+2=3=\dim\mathbb{R}^3$。求导 $D:P_n\to P_n$（$n\ge1$，$P_n$ 为次数不超过 $n$ 的多项式，维数 $n+1$）：$\ker D$ 是常数多项式，维数 1；$\operatorname{Im}D=P_{n-1}$，维数 $n$；$1+n=n+1$。两例都说明右边是定义域的维数，而不是到达域的维数。

最后看不变子空间与矩阵形状。若 $W_0\subseteq V$ 满足 $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$，取 $W_0$ 的基 $w_1,\dots,w_k$ 并扩充为 $V$ 的基 $w_1,\dots,w_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$。对 $j\le k$，$T(w_j)\in W_0$，故其在 $v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ 方向的坐标全为零，矩阵的前 $k$ 列下方为零块，呈
$$\begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
反之，若矩阵关于某组基呈此分块形状，则前 $k$ 个基向量张成的子空间在 $T$ 下不变。还要注意：维数定理的证明用了 $V$ 的有限基，无限维时不能直接套用，且单射与满射的等价链会失效；例如右移算子 $(x_1,x_2,\dots)\mapsto(0,x_1,x_2,\dots)$ 单射但不满射，左移算子满射但不单射。
en:
Let $V,W$ be vector spaces over a field and $T:V\to W$ linear. The kernel and image are
$$\ker T=\{\alpha\in V:T(\alpha)=\boldsymbol{0}\},\qquad \operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}.$$
The kernel is a subspace of $V$: $T(\boldsymbol{0})=\boldsymbol{0}$, and $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=\boldsymbol{0}$. The image is a subspace of $W$: $kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=T(k\alpha+l\beta)$ is again an image. The number $\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ is the rank of $T$ and $\dim\ker T$ is its nullity.

Rank–nullity theorem: if $V$ is finite-dimensional with $\dim V=n$, then
$$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n.$$
Proof: let $\dim\ker T=k$ and take a basis $u_1,\dots,u_k$ of the kernel; extend it by the basis extension theorem to a basis $u_1,\dots,u_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ of $V$. First, $T(v_1),\dots,T(v_{n-k})$ span $\operatorname{Im}T$: for $T(x)$ write $x=\sum a_i u_i+\sum b_j v_j$, then $T(x)=\sum b_jT(v_j)$. Second, they are independent: if $\sum c_jT(v_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$, then $T(\sum c_jv_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$, so $\sum c_jv_j\in\ker T$ and equals $\sum a_i u_i$; independence of the basis of $V$ forces all $c_j=0$. Hence they form a basis of $\operatorname{Im}T$, so $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n-k$ and the theorem follows.

The matrix version is the same statement in coordinates. An $m\times n$ matrix $A$ defines $T_A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, $T_A(\boldsymbol{x})=A\boldsymbol{x}$. Here $\operatorname{Im}T_A=\{A\boldsymbol{x}:\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\}=\operatorname{Col}(A)$, so $\dim\operatorname{Im}T_A=r(A)$, while $\ker T_A=N(A)$ is exactly the solution space of the homogeneous system. Substituting into the theorem gives
$$r(A)+\dim N(A)=n,\qquad \dim N(A)=n-r(A).$$
The right-hand side is $n$ (the number of columns and unknowns), not $m$ (the number of rows and equations); this is the most common point to misremember.

The theorem yields tests for injectivity and surjectivity. $T$ is injective iff $\ker T=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$: if $T$ is injective and $T(\alpha)=0=T(0)$, then $\alpha=0$; conversely, if the kernel is zero and $T(\alpha)=T(\beta)$, then $T(\alpha-\beta)=0$, so $\alpha=\beta$. $T$ is surjective iff $\operatorname{Im}T=W$, which in finite dimension is equivalent to $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W$. When $\dim V=\dim W=n<\infty$, combining this with $\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n$ gives: injective $\iff\dim\ker T=0\iff\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n\iff$ surjective $\iff T$ invertible. For finite-dimensional spaces of different dimensions this chain fails: injectivity and surjectivity no longer imply each other.

Two models confirm the bookkeeping. The projection $P:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$, $P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$: $\ker P=\{(0,0,z)\}$ is the $z$-axis of dimension 1; $\operatorname{Im}P=\{(x,y,0)\}$ is the $xy$-plane of dimension 2; $1+2=3=\dim\mathbb{R}^3$. The derivative $D:P_n\to P_n$ ($n\ge1$; polynomials of degree at most $n$, dimension $n+1$): $\ker D$ is the constant polynomials, dimension 1; $\operatorname{Im}D=P_{n-1}$, dimension $n$; $1+n=n+1$. Both examples show that the right-hand side is the dimension of the domain, not of the codomain.

Finally, invariant subspaces and matrix shape. If $W_0\subseteq V$ satisfies $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$, take a basis $w_1,\dots,w_k$ of $W_0$ and extend it to a basis $w_1,\dots,w_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ of $V$. For $j\le k$, $T(w_j)\in W_0$, so its coordinates in the $v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ directions all vanish; the first $k$ columns of the matrix therefore have a zero block below, giving
$$\begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
Conversely, if the matrix has this block form with respect to some basis, the span of the first $k$ basis vectors is invariant under $T$. Note also that the proof of the dimension theorem uses a finite basis of $V$; in infinite dimension it cannot be applied directly, and the equivalence of injectivity and surjectivity fails: the right shift $(x_1,x_2,\dots)\mapsto(0,x_1,x_2,\dots)$ is injective but not surjective, while the left shift is surjective but not injective.
